verses.text: For the music director. A psalm of the sons of Korah. Hear this, all you nations. Listen, everyone who lives in the world,
both ordinary people and important people, rich and poor alike.
My mouth will speak words of wisdom. My heart will speak with understanding.
I will listen carefully to a wise saying. I will explain my riddle while playing the harp.
Why should I be afraid when trouble comes, when wicked people who want to trip me up surround me?
They trust in their wealth and boast about how rich they are.
But no one can pay to save another person's life. No one can pay God a ransom for someone.
The price to save a life is too high. No payment is ever enough
to let someone live forever and never see the grave.
Everyone can see that wise people die. Foolish and stupid people also die, and they leave their wealth to others.
They think their houses will last forever, that their homes will last for all generations. They even name their lands after themselves.
But people, even with all their riches, do not last. They are like the animals that die.
This is what happens to those who trust in themselves, and to those who agree with what they say. Selah.
Like sheep they are headed for the grave. Death will be their shepherd. In the morning honest people will rule over them. Their bodies will rot in the grave, far from their fine homes.
But God will rescue me from the power of the grave. He will surely take me to himself. Selah.
Do not be upset when someone becomes rich, when the wealth of their house grows.
When they die, they will take nothing with them. Their wealth will not go down with them.
While they lived, they thought they were blessed, and people praise you when you do well for yourself.
But they will join their ancestors, who will never see the light again.
People who have riches but no understanding are like the animals that die.
